title: Microsecond token breadcrumbs instrumentation and cache-penalty accounting
creator: Marco Chen
description: Implement a high-resolution per-token tracing and accounting mechanism ("breadcrumbs") that links model emission timing, kernel execution slices, and KV cache result hits to a per-request cost/latency ledger. Goal is to enable precise root-cause and cost attribution for SLO investigations and cost optimization recommendations. This ticket covers span/schema design, low-overhead capture in the serving runtime, safe sampling strategies, pipeline enrichment, aggregation keys, and dashboard surface for debugging and automated alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a 'token_breadcrumb' span for >=95% of production requests when sampling=on with tags: request_id, causal_token_id, seq_index, delta_us, cache_hit(boolean), kernel_tag, model_version, device_type, batch_size, queue_wait_us

End-to-end pipeline ingests breadcrumb events into observability back-end (OTLP -> Kafka -> aggregation jobs) and populates the token_cost_daily view with per-request token deltas and cache-penalty attribution

New dashboard 'Token Breadcrumbs — Latency & Cost' exists in Console showing: per-request percentile token_delta_us, cache_hit vs miss latency distribution, and top-20 kernel contributors by p99 token delta
Sampling knobs exist: 0%/0.1%/1%/10% with consistent trace linking to request-level spans; enabling sampling=100% in staging does not exceed CPU budget in the serving pod by more than 7% in load test
Automated alert: if median token_delta_us increases by >50% for a specific model_version or device_type over 15 minutes, triggers PagerDuty with contextual span links
Design doc and span schema published with backwards-compatible fields and migratable storage format
tasks: Design span schema and serialization format (compact binary + optional json envelope)
Add token breadcrumb emitter to runtime after KV cache lookup and after kernel emission step
Implement sampling policy and deterministic sampling hash based on request_id
Extend OTLP exporter to batch token breadcrumbs to Kafka topic 'telemetry.token_breadcrumbs'
Create aggregation job to join breadcrumbs with request metadata and compute per-request token-attribution ledger
Build Console dashboard panels and alert rules, wire to existing token-level SLO dashboards
Run 72-hour staging soak with sampling=10% and capture perf delta metrics
Document signal definitions and onboarding notes for support and SRE teams
technical_design: We will introduce a minimal 'token_breadcrumb' span with fields kept flat and compact to limit overhead. Each breadcrumb is emitted at two points: immediately after KV cache resolution (cache_probe) and after the kernel returns logits for a token group (kernel_emit). Breadcrumb fields: request_id, trace_id, seq_index (int), causal_token_id (uuid4 short), delta_us (int microseconds), event_type (cache_probe | kernel_emit), cache_hit (bool), kernel_tag (string), model_version (string), device_type (string), batch_size (int), mem_pressure_level (string), timestamp_iso. To avoid high cardinality we enforce tag canonicalization for kernel_tag and device_type and use integer enums in binary encoding. Emission uses an async lock-free ring buffer per worker thread and a lightweight binary envelope that is flushed to the OTLP exporter in batches. Backpressure policy: if ring buffer is full, drop non-kernel_emit cache_probe events and increment dropped_breadcrumbs counter per worker. Sampling is deterministic using fnv1a(request_id) % 10000 < sampling_rate_basispoints. Staging will validate that this approach provides sub-5% CPU overhead at 10% sampling on our p4d equivalent testbed. Aggregation will join breadcrumbs by request_id and seq_index and compute deltas: kernel_time = kernel_emit.delta_us - cache_probe.delta_us (when both present). Cache-penalty attribution is recorded as token_cache_savings_us = if cache_hit true then (median_kernel_emit_without_cache - kernel_emit.delta_us) computed offline via baseline experiments. Aggregation outputs per-request rows: request_id, model_version, total_tokens, total_kernel_us, total_cache_us_saved_estimate, p95_token_delta_us. These feed Console analytics and cost models.
telemetry_schema: Event name: token_breadcrumb. Fields (flat): request_id, trace_id, seq_index, causal_token_id, event_type, delta_us, cache_hit, kernel_tag, model_version, device_type, batch_size, mem_pressure_level, timestamp_iso, sampling_rate_basispoints, dropped_reason(optional). All fields must be strings or integers in the exporter; in our JSON envelope we map enums to human names for debugging. Export path: OTLP->Kafka topic 'telemetry.token_breadcrumbs' partitioned by trace_id hash. Aggregation consumer writes to 'token_breadcrumbs_agg' timeseries table (daily partition) and materialized view 'token_cost_daily' for analytics. Retention: raw breadcrumbs 7 days; aggregated views 365 days. Metrics emitted: telemetry.token_breadcrumbs.emitted, .dropped, .export_latency_ms, .aggregate_job_lag_ms.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable sampling=100% on staging cluster for 72h, validate schema, ensure exporter throughput, and full aggregation correctness. Phase 2 (canary): enable sampling=1% on 5% of production traffic routing via sampling hash. Monitor CPU/RAM/p99 latencies and exporter lag. Phase 3 (ramp): move to 10% across more regions for 1 week. Phase 4 (SOS): limited 100% traces for targeted customers with opt-in via feature flag. Final: flip default sampling to 0.1% and provide self-serve knob in Console. Each phase must pass a perf gate: exporter backpressure <1%, additional CPU <10% per pod, aggregate job lag <2m.
risks_mitigation: High-cardinality tags (kernel_tag/model_version) — mitigate by canonicalization and enum mapping before export
Exporter overload — use batching and backpressure counters; implement quota and drop strategy for cache_probe non-critical events
Storage blow-up — limit raw retention to 7 days and store aggregated views instead
Observable blind spots from sampling — provide deterministic sampling and targeted 100% traces for SRE investigations
False cache-penalty estimates — baseline kernels in controlled experiments and store model-versioned baselines
notes: Design trade-off: binary envelope reduces payload size but complicates ad-hoc query; to balance we include a small json debug payload on sampled events (1 in 1000) that contains human-readable tags
We should coordinate with billing team to validate that token_cost_daily output maps sensibly to per-token billing models before using for chargeback
SRE asked for an emergency toggle to disable breadcrumb emission entirely across fleet via remote config
